 ORDER IA No. 22646/2023, an application under Section 301(2) Cr.P.C. is taken up, considered and allowed for the reasons mentioned therein.
Shri Nishant Sharma and his associates are permitted to assist the prosecution.

This first bail application has been filed by applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.313/2023 registered at Police Station Fatehgarh, District Guna (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of the IPC.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 25/10/2023.

sentences.text: Guna on 18/10/2023 at 23.59 that on the same day around 7.30 pm, her husband alongwith his friend Anil had come to her home.
Her husband went to take vegetables from house of her mother-in- law.
Thereafter, Anil gagged her mouth and pushed her on the ground and committed rape on her.
Meanwhile her husband returned and opened the door, accused- Anil fled away.
She narrated the incident to her husband and mother- in-law.
On such allegations, Police Station Fatehgarh, District Guna registered FIR at Crime No. 313/2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of the IPC.
Prosecutrix was forwarded for medico-legal examination.
No sign of use of force was found in the medico-legal examination.
Statements of prosecutrix and witnesses were recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C.
Statement of prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
Applicant was arrested on 25/10/2023, he is in custody ever since.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that it is a matter of consensual relationship.
Applicant is falsely implicated in this matter under pressure of husband of the prosecutrix.
Applicant is aged 19 years.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of his abconsion leaving behind his family and home.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the evidence by the applicant.
Jail incarceration on false allegations is causing hardship to applicant.
The trial would take time to complete.

Therefore,
applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and prays for its rejection.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the complainant submits that complainant has no objection to grant of bail, as it was a matter of consensual relationship.
It is further stated that complainant has made false complaint under pressure.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
